title: Files
summary: Attaching files to records, sharing them with a customer, and where they are stored on disk.
html:
Files can be attached to a customer, a job, a quote, an invoice or a ticket. A file attached to a record is found by opening the record, which is the point — contracts and specifications stop living in email.

Uploading

Open the record and use the file area. Several files can be uploaded at once. Each one can carry a description, which is worth filling in; a folder of scan_0041.pdf is not searchable by anyone.

Sharing with a customer

A file can be marked visible to the customer, which makes it downloadable in the portal. Files are private unless you share them.

You can also email a file directly from its record, which sends a link rather than an attachment — so large files do not bounce.

Buckets

A bucket is a named group of files that is not tied to one record. Use it for things that apply to many customers: a standard terms document, a price list, a logo pack.

Where files go on disk

Uploads are written to the application's own storage folder, not into the database. That has two consequences worth knowing:

  • Back up the files as well as the database. A database-only backup restores the list of files and none of the files. See Backups.
  • The folder has to be writable by the web server. If uploads fail with no obvious error, that is the first thing to check — see Troubleshooting.

Upload limits

The largest file you can upload is set by PHP, not by this application: upload_max_filesize and post_max_size. Most shared hosting defaults to a few megabytes. Configuration covers where to change them.
